title: Mirror verification patterns and TF interface hacks
content:
Purpose:
This is a working notes doc for patterns we've been experimenting with to verify mirrored artifacts in isolated sites, plus pragmatic Terraform module interface 'hacks' to make seeding and upgrades safe in air-gapped environments. Aim: capture reproducible verification steps, a small set of TF inputs/outputs we actually want, and borderline automation we can ship as examples (not productionized yet).

Scope and assumptions:
- Target: small-to-medium on-prem clusters (1-4 racks) where a local registry + cache proxies are used.
- We assume no persistent internet access during install/upgrade operations.
- Operators can physically deliver media (USB/portable SSD) if necessary (sneakernet fallback).
- We rely on standard OCI images and Helm charts for runtime components; some tooling will need to handle tarballs for non-OCI artifacts (e.g., plugin bundles).

High-level approach (one-liner):
1) Curate deterministic artifact list -> 2) Mirror + sign -> 3) Produce signed index manifest -> 4) Seed registry or import tarball -> 5) Verify digests & smoke-run -> 6) Apply TF with pinned digests -> 7) Run staged upgrade with verification gates.

Concrete playbook (operator flow):
- Step 0: prep workspace on bastion with reproducible env (docker 24.x, skopeo, crane, cosign, gpg). Record OS + tool versions.
- Step 1: artifact list generation
  - Start from dev manifest (repo: infra/artifact-lists) and reduce to site-needed set. Use a lockfile approach: artifacts.lock (format: newline-separated entries -> TYPE|NAME|TAG|DIGEST|SOURCE_URL). Example line: "oci|redwood/runtime|v2.4.1|sha256:aaa...|ghcr.io/redwood/runtime:v2.4.1"
  - TODO: canonicalize how charts vs OCI vs raw tarballs are recorded.
- Step 2: mirror and capture digests
  - For OCI images: use skopeo copy --all to mirror into local registry staging (registry:5000). Capture digest after copy (crane digest OR skopeo inspect).
  - For charts: helm pull --untar + tar -> convert to OCI via helm chart save (if OCI capable), else keep chart tarball. Compute sha256 of file.
  - For plugin/agent bundles (non-OCI): bundle.tar.gz + accompanying manifest.json (bundles MUST include a provenance.txt).
  - Save a site-locked manifest with exact digests: site-manifest.json (but plain text lockfile ok).
- Step 3: sign artifacts and index
  - Sign the site lockfile with cosign keypair (preferred) or GPG (fallback). Store signature alongside index. Format: index-v1.tar.gz + index-v1.sig.
  - Consider embedding a signed mapping file that maps logical names to digests (helps reconciliation later).
- Step 4: produce seed: two delivery modes
  - Online seed (if limited outbound allowed): push to seeded registry in target VPC using TLS + auth.
  - Offline seed (airgap): produce OCI distributable tarball (crane export OR registry-export tool) OR create filesystem layout for registry-import. Tarball must include index, blobs/, manifests/, and signatures. Label with semantic name: redwood-site-seed-<site>-<iso-date>.tar.gz
- Step 5: import and verify on target site
  - Import tarball using registry-import script (small python helper that uses registry API to push blobs).
  - Run verification: for each entry in site-manifest, pull by digest and validate digest and signature. Run container image smoke-run for key services (run image with --rm and check /health endpoint).
  - Keep an artifacts.audit log (timestamped lines: DIGEST|TYPE|OK|SMOKE-TEST-RESULT|NOTES).

Terraform module interface recommendations (practical, intentionally minimal):
- Goals: make module inputs stable and allow pinning by digest; avoid forcing users to hand-edit many variables during airgap.
- Inputs we actually need:
  - local_registry_host (string) -- e.g., "host.local:5000"
  - image_pins (map(string)) -- map of logical name -> digest (sha256:...); modules use digest-pinned image references
  - chart_assets_bucket (string) -- for places we boot from object store during install preparation (optional)
  - seed_manifest_ref (string) -- reference to seed index: e.g., "git+ssh://...#path=site-manifests/foo-lockfile" OR a local path when running offline
  - seed_mode (string) -- "import_tar" | "push" | "none"
- Outputs we want:
  - applied_pins (map) -- the digest map the module actually used
  - import_job_id (string) -- id of any async import job run by module helpers (if we support it)
- Interface 'hack' patterns we've used:
  - Provide a simple hook script variable: preseed_hook (string, path) that TF will call via null_resource local-exec. The hook does the heavy lifting (import, checks). This keeps TF simple and avoids embedding complex logic in HCL.
  - Keep schema changes additive: avoid requiring plan-time network access to resolve digests. Accept a precomputed image_pins map so plan/apply are deterministic.
  - When possible, treat the registry as "immutable" once seeded for a given release tag. For upgrades, new seed manifests with incremented release versions are imported side-by-side and then the module triggers rollout.

Upgrade strategy (staged, verification-driven):
- Canary semantics: rollout to a narrow pool (e.g., 10% of nodes or staging ASG) that uses new digests.
- Verification gates (examples):
  - probe pass rate >= 99% for 15m
  - no increase in 5xx or retries in request traces (compare to baseline)
  - latency p95 delta < +50ms (site-specific)
- Automated rollback: if verification gate fails, TF triggers a rollback by applying previous applied_pins map and scaling back. We prefer to implement rollback orchestration in the ops/agent layer rather than full Terraform-driven process because TF is slow to react.

Edge cases and gotchas we've hit (notes):
- Skipping image layer checks can lead to subtle corruption during copy; always verify sha256 after push and compare to upstream digest (if available).
- A local registry may rewrite manifest references (e.g., when registry supports content-digest rewriting). Insist we pin by digest, not by tag, in TF and runtime deploys.
- Some registries reject manifests with unknown mediaType for indexes -> we saw this with older distribution code. Need to include a compatibility mapping step in the import helper.
- Helm charts that include external download URLs (e.g., wget in templates) must be rewritten to local URLs or vendorized; add a preflight transform step.

Minimum verification checklist (operator runbook snippet):
- [ ] confirm seed manifest signature matches COSIGN key
- [ ] import tarball into registry (or push images)
- [ ] for each pinned digest: docker pull registry:5000/name@sha256:<digest>
- [ ] validate digest with "crane digest" or skopeo inspect
- [ ] run container smoke-run for runtime (script: tests/smoke-run.sh <image>)
- [ ] run helm dry-run for charts using local registry endpoints
- [ ] collect artifacts.audit and upload to central audit-store (if allowed)

Automation primitives and scripts (sketches):
- scripts/mirror-site.sh (uses skopeo/crane, produces artifacts.lock and site-seed.tar.gz)
- scripts/import-registry.py (reads site-seed.tar.gz and pushes blobs to registry API)
- scripts/verify-seed.sh (consumes artifacts.lock and runs digest checks + smoke tests)
- Provide examples under infra/examples/airgap/<site-name>/ containing image_pins.tfvars and seed_manifest.json

Open questions / TODOs:
- We need a standard format for artifacts.lock that supports both OCI & non-OCI assets (proposal: CSV with TYPE field). Agree on it? (RACI: Marco to propose by 2026-03-10).
- How do we rotate cosign keys for long-lived sites without internet (k8s operator for local key rotation vs manual process)?
- Should we add a small registry shim that accepts our index tarball and does the import to avoid writing registry-import python tool? Tradeoff: more infra vs simpler operator UX.
- Investigate using Notary V2 for provenance tracking; cosign is fine for now but spec alignment is desirable.

References and breadcrumbs:
- Confluence draft: AIRGAP-architecture-draft (linked above)
- Jira: JIRA-2148 (airgap seeding MVP)
- Example PR: github.com/redwood-inference/release-tools/pull/452 (proof-of-concept import tool)
- Slack threads: #private-deploys "airgap-import-smoke" (search for thread id in channel)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the TF module tiny. Mixed feelings about null_resource local-exec but it's pragmatic for now.
- For any customer pilot, we should ship the scripts as a small tarball with a README + example.tfvars so SEs can run it in 30-60m.
- When packaging the site-seed, include a VERSION file with tool versions to help reproduce issues.

Appendix A: minimal artifacts.lock example (lines):
oci|redwood/runtime|v2.4.1|sha256:aaa111...|ghcr.io/redwood/runtime:v2.4.1
chart|redwood/console|1.3.0|sha256:bbb222...|https://charts.redwood:443/console-1.3.0.tgz
bundle|agent-plugins|20251001|sha256:ccc333...|s3://redwood-bundles/site-x/agent-plugins-20251001.tar.gz

Appendix B: quick local checks (commands):
- skopeo copy docker://ghcr.io/redwood/runtime:v2.4.1 docker://local-reg:5000/redwood/runtime:v2.4.1 --all
- crane digest local-reg:5000/redwood/runtime:v2.4.1
- cosign sign --key cosign.key artifacts.lock
- python3 scripts/import-registry.py --tar site-seed.tar.gz --registry https://local-reg:5000 --insecure-skip-tls

End of doc.

Revision notes: first working draft; expect to convert artifacts.lock to a structured JSON or CSV during iteration.
